entities.summary:
Jean Toomer was an American poet and novelist commonly associated with modernism and the Harlem Renaissance, though he actively resisted the latter association. His reputation stems from his novel Cane (1923), which Toomer wrote during and after a stint as a school principal at a black school in rural Sparta, Georgia. The novel intertwines the stories of six women and includes an apparently autobiographical thread; sociologist Charles S.

Johnson called it "the most astonishingly brilliant beginning of any Negro writer of his generation". Jean Toomer was a writers & intellectuals from Washington, D.C. (1894-12-26, Washington, D.C.–1967-03-30). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Jean Toomer's novel Cane (1923) is notable for its representation of African American experiences and its influence on modernist literature. The book has been recognized as a significant work in the Harlem Renaissance, with sociologist Charles S. Johnson praising it as 'the most astonishingly brilliant beginning of any Negro writer of his generation'.
